It's surprisingly difficult to inventory a farm.

There are 60ish cows (and four bulls). There are an untold number of bacons and baby bacons. There are six horses - plus the horses that board which do not belong to me. There are two oxen that get to pull stuff at the local county fairs. There are some turkeys, a couple of ducks and geese, and other assorted stuff.

It's pretty much your typical multi-faceted rural New England farm. There's an indoor and outdoor riding arena and people rent those, give lessons, or rent horses and ride the trails, or they board horses. The two primary income sources are boarding and milk. They do well at the local farmer's market. In the fall, they process game. That sort of thing - it's pretty much a stereotypical farm like you're envisioning. Much of it is wooded, 'cause it's, you know, Maine. They don't do large grain crops or anything. They do sell quite a bit of hay. I think that might have been third highest revenue.

Inventorying a farm is not an easy task. I ended up hiring a specialist company and the books will be kept by yet another specialist company. My regular accountant wants nothing to do with it.
